chapter: Bebop, Tadd Dameron, Slam Stewart and Europe
title: Tadd Dameron, bass lines and the Woodside Hotel
summary: Collins corrected Tadd Dameron's bass lines before the war, and on his return Dameron repaid him by showing him bebop on an organ.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: 1946. So Tadd Dameron, here we go. When I first met Tadd it was before I went in the army. Tadd came to New York to write for Lunceford, and we used to meet every night at the Woodside. We'd get high, we'd play, and you know -- so he would play these things, some of the arrangements he had for Lunceford and I would tell him, look, Tadd your ideas are beautiful but your bassline is wrong. So he said what do you mean, and so I would take just what he did and I'd play a different bassline, you know, and show him just where the beauty of the bass, you know, here. The bass should go this way, the bass tells the story, you know. And he never forgot that.

When I came out of the army, the whole scene had changed musically, so Tadd came and got me, and he said, come on, go to my hotel room, I want to show you something. So we had a little organ and he sat down and he started playing, he said this is the way things are going. And we would sit there all night and I would just listen and he would just play. And now, look, this is what has happened. He did this out of appreciation. He never forgot what I did for him. He said, here. So he would just play, he would just -- and I would
just absorb. So then I get my guitar --
